Where does the price action over the past few months leave us in terms of the secular bull market? In my view (which is in the minority) the secular bull started in 2009, which means that at age 17 it is very mature. Rising margins and valuations have been drivers of the bull, and neither suggests that it’s over. But a low cost of capital and a healthy payout caused by de-equitization have also been drivers, and those are well past their inflection points.

The majority of Americans are not saving enough for their retirement:

Just 14% of participants in Vanguard-managed 401(k) plans contributed the maximum to their plans in 2025.

Among those earning $150,000 or more, 51% contributed the maximum, compared with 10% of those earning between $100,000 and $149,999.

Meanwhile, just 2% of those earning $75,000-$99,999 and 1% of those earning $50,000-$74,999 contributed the maximum last year.

Fewer than 0.5% of participants earning below $50,000 reached the annual limit.

Among age groups, 10% of workers aged 25-34 maxed out their 401(k) contributions in 2025, compared with 15% of those aged 35-44 and 17% of those aged 45-54.

The highest proportion was recorded among workers aged 55-64, at 19%, followed by 18% seen among those aged 65 and older.

Most Americans are struggling to build adequate retirement savings.

BREAKING: China’s non-monetary gold imports rose to a record $209.0 billion in the first 10 months of the year.

This represents a record ~8% of China’s total imports over the same period.

By comparison, full-year 2025 gold imports totaled $96.5 billion.

In October alone, China’s gold imports surged +174% YoY, to 155.9 tonnes.

In Dollar terms, the value of these imports jumped +184% YoY, to $20.7 billion.

As a result, gold became China's 3rd-largest import category by value in October, behind only memory chips and crude oil.

China is accumulating gold at an unprecedented pace.

The market has repriced the number of rate hikes from three to two, and even December is now priced at 90%. Much like the fourth quarter of 2018 when a 20% drawdown forced the Fed to pivot from tightening to easing, a Fed pivot now seems like the only put option available if the current liquidation goes much further. During the Tariff Tantrum the pivot was as simple as the White House capitulating on the threat of tariffs, but this time it will have to be a monetary policy pivot leading to easier financial conditions. With a hot economy in which neither of the Fed’s mandates justify easing, this might be easier said than done.

Banking conditions are tightening in the US:

A net 30% of leaders from the banking sector and lending institutions across the Fed's 8th District reported lower loan demand in the current quarter, according to the Fed Economic Conditions Survey.

This marks a sharp deterioration from the previous quarter, when a net 11% of respondents reported higher loan demand.

Meanwhile, a net 7% of respondents expect loan demand to decline further next quarter.

A net 13% reported that credit standards tightened this quarter and expect them to tighten further next quarter.

And, a net 28% reported an increase in delinquencies this quarter, while a net 25% expect delinquencies to increase further next quarter.

Tighter lending standards pressuring loan and investment demand.

Market leadership has shifted:

Apple, $AAPL, has outperformed Nvidia, $NVDA, by 30.2 percentage points so far in November, putting it on track for its largest monthly outperformance since the 2008 Financial Crisis.

This comes as $NVDA is down -27.0% over this period, while $AAPL is up +3.2% and is trading near its all-time high.

This would also mark the 4th-largest monthly outperformance by Apple since Nvidia's IPO in January 1999.

Since October 1st, $AAPL has outperformed $NVDA by 44.1 percentage points, putting it on track for its largest 2-month outperformance since July 2011.

$AAPL is also on pace to finish higher in 7 of the last 8 months and is up +31.3% year-to-date.

Apple has quietly become one of the biggest beneficiaries of the recent market rotation.

The chart of the semiconductor index shows that the semis double-topped just as the fast money came pouring in. A classic technical occurrence of rising enthusiasm not being enough to move the needle, followed by a distribution top that traps those longs.  Since those flows have not reversed, it may take some time for this sector to find its footing. The good news is that the index has now reached its double-top price target, so perhaps this will stop the bleeding.

Back in the days charts were more clear... we hear a lot right?

Correct. With computerized trading, Global access and funds/market makers price action became more volatile. Breakouts are not as clean as before...

I agree. But this is the case in the widely traded names. 

Nothing stops you to search the non-popular names. The price charts are as clean as the old days. You don't need to trade NVDA, META or AMD. 

As breakout traders we are after directional movement no matter where.

I worked at different parts of the financial industry.

Analyst at a leading brokerage firm.
Analyst/fund manager, portfolio manager at semi-sovereign funds.
Portfolio manager at family offices.

I can tell you with confidence, the most advantaged individuals in financial sector are "part-time retail traders".

Note: if you are disciplined with great self control and operate not with instincts but with predefined rules, do not need to follow markets intraday, do not need more than 1 screen to run research and place orders, have the flexibility to step out of your office and engage in non-finance activities you are way ahead and with more clear mind than the trader who sits in front of 4 screens that are connected to a Bloomberg terminal.

For me the simple strategy is based on capturing trend periods out of well-defined consolidations. In this, I focus on breakouts through horizontal boundaries with min 3 touch points. No indicators. No volume. Pure price action out of a well-defined consolidation.

A sound risk management should have "on average" $ win / $ loss > 4 and can be profitable with win rates between 35%-45%. The asymmetry in finding setups to capture directional movement should aim these.
